name: Metro car
intro: The metro car. It stops everywhere and asks nothing. Getting off at the right stop is up to me.

readables.name: STAFF DOOR
pages: STAFF ONLY. LOCKED.
NO PASSENGER ACCESS.

readables.name: NOTICE
pages: CAMERAS OPERATE IN THIS CAR.
RECORDINGS ARE KEPT FOR THE DURATION OF THE PASSENGER PLUS 90 DAYS.

readables.name: TO CAR 2
pages: CAR 2 · LOCKED.
INTER-CAR TRAVEL SUSPENDED UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE.

readables.name: MAN IN A SUIT
pages: I have a meeting at Galleria.
I have had it for six loops now. It keeps getting moved to the next stop.
readables.label: [E] TALK

readables.name: COURIER
pages: Parcel for "whoever is at the Harbor". That is the whole address.
I ride round until somebody looks like a whoever.
readables.label: [E] TALK

readables.name: OLD WOMAN
pages: That brake? I pulled it once. Forty years ago. They still send me a letter every birthday.
You have to register an emergency two days ahead now. Nobody plans an emergency.
Well. Some people do.
readables.label: [E] TALK

readables.name: PUNK
pages: They check IDs at every exit now.
So I never get off. Checkmate.
readables.label: [E] TALK

pages: End of shift. Fourteen parcels, zero complaints, one sore back.
Downtown is next. Then bed.
← → walk. E talks to people.
touchPages: End of shift. Fourteen parcels, zero complaints, one sore back.
The arrows at the bottom walk. Tap someone to talk.
intro.speaker: YOU

pages: Morning shift?
Me too. Mine started yesterday. The meeting keeps getting moved to the next stop.
Night shift? You have the look. Like a receipt somebody kept.
Me, I am on my ninth loop with a parcel for "whoever is at the Harbor". Still no whoever.
Downtown next, dear. Then Galleria. Then Downtown.
I have ridden this line since it was a straight line.
Get some sleep. You look registered, but tired.
They retired a thousand records overnight. It was on the screen.
Retired. Like they get a watch and a cake.
